skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At T2, at the very start, the interviewer said 'we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.'

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explained that the privilege 'belongs to the company, not to you or to us,' that the company decides whether to waive it, and that it may disclose what is learned 'without your consent and without telling you.'

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 explained how the interview would proceed, asked for complete answers, told the witness to flag speculation, estimates and assumptions, and asked whether he was remembering or reconstructing. Rapport and tone were thin.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asked 'Do you understand? Do you have any questions?' and T4 asked the witness to restate who was represented and who controls privilege; T5 confirmed it.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T64 asked whether anything else should be known, T66 asked who else to speak with, and T68 covered keeping documents, confidentiality, not discussing with other witnesses, possible follow-up, and 'Anything to add or correct?'

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
Throughout, please tell me whether you actually remember something or are reconstructing it, and say so if you're unsure.
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: T14 invited 'Tell me everything you remember' and T16 followed up, but most later questions were narrow and closed, leaving little room for the witness to walk through events.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Moved from role (T8) to an open LJM1 narrative (T14) to specifics (T18-T21), then to Southampton and Chewco in a sensible order.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions were single and clear, such as T20 'Who raised it with them first?'. T42 combined three names in one question and T56 presumed the answer.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Polite and in control throughout, including when the witness gave terse answers such as T3 and T5.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: Adjusted to answers: T24 asked 'How sure are you', T38 put the $4.5 million figure to the witness, T44 restated his position, and T62-T63 followed up on approval sheets. It did not return to the witness's reference to the minutes at T25.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Who raised it with them first?
Did you tell the Board, Mr. Lay, or Mr. Skilling about the Foundation's investment?
How do you know Mr. Causey and Mr. Buy reviewed every LJM2 deal?

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Followed up on evasive answers: T34-T38 moved from 'A small amount' to a specific figure, and T40-T45 tested the Board disclosure against the Foundation's investment. It did not challenge T19 'It was discussed with Ken and Jeff' or T25 'It's in the minutes'.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Established who (the Foundation, Kopper) and how much at Southampton, but did not establish when the Foundation invested or the timing and decision-makers for the Chewco role.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: Gave a figure at T38 and used the minutes at T52, but did not try other routes when the witness said 'I'd have to check' or relied on 'It's in the minutes'.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: Separated personal knowledge from others' knowledge: T42-T45 asked who was told, and T58-T59 asked whether he checked the controls, eliciting 'Not personally.'

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: T66 asked who else to speak with and got Causey, Buy and Kopper, but the interviewer did not probe further, for example on Glisan, who was mentioned at T13.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: T60-T63 surfaced approval sheets ('The sheets would show it'), but the interviewer did not request or follow up on those sheets or other records.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: T24 'How sure are you that's what you told them?' and T58 'Did you check that it was followed?' tested certainty and the basis for the witness's knowledge.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Followed material answers: T31-T39 on the Foundation's investment, T46-T51 on disclosure considerations, and T60-T63 on approval sheets.

moments.text: Witness described the Foundation's investment as 'A small amount. It did well.'
Interviewer put roughly $4.5 million received about six weeks after investment to the witness, who said 'That sounds about right.'
How does that fit with what you told the Board about not receiving value from the Enron stock?
How sure are you that's what you told them?
Who else should we speak with?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: Showed the November 5, 1997 minutes at T52 and asked whether he recognized them, which gave minimal authentication, but gave no context for why the document was being shown.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: Before showing the minutes, asked for his account of why Kopper was chosen (T46-T51), then used the document at T52.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: Described the minutes only by asking whether they mention Kopper's role (T54) and did not describe their content. Nothing was misstated.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: T54 asked a neutral question without stating a conclusion about the document.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: After the witness said 'No' at T55, the interviewer did not put his earlier disclosure explanations (T49-T51) against the minutes or invite him to explain the difference.

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
Do they mention Mr. Kopper's role in Chewco?
No.

missed_opportunities: T55: After the witness said 'No' about whether the minutes mention Kopper's role, the interviewer did not put his earlier disclosure explanation (T49-T51) against the minutes or ask him to reconcile them.

T25: The witness said 'It's in the minutes' about what he told the Board, and the interviewer did not use the minutes to test that claim. The witness's account at T21 that he raised the GP role with Ken and Jeff was also not followed up on who else was present.
tips: What did the June 28, 1999 Board materials say about your economics, and how does the Foundation's investment fit with that statement?
The minutes do not name Mr. Kopper's role in Chewco, so what explanation do you have for that, given the disclosure considerations you raised earlier?
